gloss: shou (traditional unit of volume, approx. 1.8 liters)

definitions.gloss: shou; traditional Japanese unit of volume equal to approximately 1.8 liters
definitions.explanation: A traditional unit of measurement in the Japanese system. One shou equals approximately 1.8 liters and is still commonly used when measuring rice and sake. Ten shou make one to (斗).

examples.japanese: {米|こめ}を{一升|いっしょう}{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought one shou of rice.

examples.japanese: {一升瓶|いっしょうびん}の{日本酒|にほんしゅ}をもらった。
examples.english: I received a one-shou bottle of sake.

examples.japanese: {餅|もち}つきには{三升|さんじょう}の{米|こめ}を{用意|ようい}する{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: We plan to prepare three shou of rice for the mochi pounding.

notes:
A traditional unit of volume in the Japanese measuring system ({尺貫法|しゃっかんほう}). One {升|しょう} equals approximately 1.8 liters (about 1.9 US quarts). Still widely used in everyday life for measuring {米|こめ} (rice) and {日本酒|にほんしゅ} (sake).

MEASUREMENT SYSTEM:
- {一合|いちごう} = approximately 180 ml
- {一升|いっしょう} = 10 {合|ごう} = approximately 1.8 liters
- {一斗|いっと} = 10 {升|しょう} = approximately 18 liters

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一升瓶|いっしょうびん}: 1.8-liter bottle (standard sake bottle size)
- {一升|いっしょう}{炊|だ}き: rice cooker that holds one shou
- {升|ます}: the wooden measuring box itself (also read as ます)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The wooden {升|ます} box used to measure one {升|しょう} is a symbol of prosperity and is sometimes used as a drinking vessel at celebrations. The word {升|ます} is a homophone of {増|ま}す (to increase), making it an auspicious item.
